subject: Private deployment — shared-infra appendix & SLO alignment
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cobalttech.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jones <alex.jones@cobalttech.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private deployment — SLO coverage for CobaltTech on-prem

Hi Kim —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re close to finalizing the PO but I need one last clarification from your side before procurement signs off.

Because our deployment will sit behind a customer-managed DMZ and transit gateway, we have several network constraints (egress NAT pool limits, strict ACLs, custom NAT timeouts). These factors mean we can’t guarantee the sub-50ms round-trip for some of our internal agents, and we’d like Redwood to confirm whether it will accept a carve-out from the latency portion of the Private SLOs (we want uptime commitments to remain standard). In practice we’re asking for an appendix that: 
- Acknowledges shared responsibility for network egress and customer-managed routing;
- Limits latency SLA claims to Redwood-controlled path segments;
- Includes recommended mitigations (eg. NAT pooling guidance, heartbeat checks, fallback model variant).

Can you point us to a draft appendix or example language you typically use for these scenarios? We also can share a sanitized network diagram if that helps.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is hoping to complete this week.

Best,
Nina Patel
VP Product Operations, CobaltTech
(attachment: cobalt-network-summary.txt (TXT, 6 KB))

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cobalttech.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — SLO coverage for CobaltTech on-prem

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear summary.

Short answer: yes — we can scope latency SLOs to Redwood-controlled path segments and provide an appendix that documents shared-responsibility boundaries. We typically call this an "Infrastructure Responsibility Appendix" and include:
- A diagram and definition of Redwood-managed vs customer-managed components;
- A clause stating latency SLOs apply only to tokens processed on our runtime (post-ingress) and exclude customer-managed network-induced tail latency;
- Operational steps for diagnosing and jointly triaging issues (trace IDs, synthetic checks, escalation matrix).

Next steps I propose:
1) If you can drop a sanitized network diagram (no IPs) to the Drive link below, Marcus and I will draft appendix language and suggested mitigations.
2) We’ll include a short table of recommended NAT settings and heartbeat frequency for your infra team.
3) If SOC will need specific evidence for SLA alignment (eg. packet capture allowances, audit logs), include a list in your reply.

I’m attaching a short template we’ve used previously and will iterate once we see your diagram.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cAppendixDraft
Attachment: (infrastructure-resp-template.pdf (PDF, 48 KB))

Thanks — I’ll loop Vivek for compliance sign-off once we have a draft.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
(attachment: infrastructure-resp-template.pdf)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment — SLO coverage for CobaltTech on-prem

Team — forwarding Nina’s ask and the drive link. Key negotiation points I think we should propose:

1) Clear definition: "Redwood-managed segment" begins at the first hop inside Redwood's ingress VPN and ends at token acceptance by runtime; anything upstream (customer NAT, transit gateway, private peering) is customer-managed.
2) Latency SLO carve-out: keep standard uptime SLO (99.95% uptime) for Private, but make latency SLOs conditional on customer meeting specific network conditions (table of egress throughput, NAT idle timeout <= 120s, route health checks).
3) Joint triage rubric: when an incident includes elevated latency, the parties agree to run a 4-step triage within 2 hours — Redwood will validate the runtime and KV cache, customer verifies egress and NAT.
4) Evidence and compliance: Vivek — can you confirm whether our SOC/audit team is comfortable with the above and whether we need to provide additional telemetry (eg. signed flow logs) to support uptime credits?

I’ve started a draft appendix in the Drive and attached a small network-diagram placeholder for Cobalt (they asked for an example of how we call things out). I’d like sign-off from Legal/Compliance before we push to the customer.

Quote (original):
> From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cobalttech.com>
> Thanks again for the walkthrough last week...

—Kim

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cobalttech.com>
Cc: Alex Jones <alex.jones@cobalttech.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: CobaltTech — Infrastructure Responsibility Appendix (for review)

Hi Nina / Alex —

Thanks for the quick response and for sharing the sanitized diagram — helpful. Attached is a draft appendix that captures the shared-responsibility language, a short table of recommended NAT/heartbeat settings, and the proposed triage matrix. High-level notes:

- Uptime SLO: unchanged (Redwood Private: 99.95% availability for runtime services).
- Latency SLO: scoped to Redwood-managed path segments only; we explicitly exclude customer-managed egress/transit from latency credit calculations.
- Mitigations: suggested NAT pooling and a recommended NAT idle timeout of 120s; optional use of our synthetic probes (we can host probes in your region if you allow a small egress ACL).
- Evidence: for any credit claim that touches shared boundaries we’ll need jointly produced timelines (trace IDs, probe runs) and the network diagram used for time-of-incident analysis.

Attachment: cobalt_shared_infra_appendix_v1.pdf (draft)
Network diagram: network-diagram-cobalttech.png
Drive (editable): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cAppendixDraft
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/78421/company/COB-2027-045

If this looks good, please comment directly in the PDF (or the Drive doc) and we’ll prepare a final version for signature. Also flag any SOC evidence requests and we’ll route to Vivek’s team.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if you’d prefer to walk through the table.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cobalttech.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jones <alex.jones@cobalttech.com>, CobaltTech SOC <soc@cobalttech.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:50:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft: CobaltTech — Infrastructure Responsibility Appendix (for review)

Kim — this looks right. Thanks for pulling together the draft and the mitigations table. A couple of minor asks from SOC:
- Can you add a short paragraph that commits to providing request-level trace IDs and a template for the joint-incident timeline?
- Confirm that synthetic probes will not contain customer payload (just timing/latency measurements).

If you can add those two clarifications we can proceed to signature (we’ll route to procurement for a DocuSign tomorrow).

Nina
VP Product Operations, CobaltTech

Onboarding note: Alex and I will attach the final signed appendix to the PO so the legal team has it inline with the contract. (attachment: cobalt-soc-requests.txt)
